title: Lab 03 — Checkout: Card Iframes, Double Clicks, Declines & Pennies

variants.hint: What does a real, impatient customer do to a slow Pay button? And are you counting what the SERVER did, or what the page says?
variants.debrief: The Pay button wasn't disabled and sent no idempotency key, so a double-click produced two charges while the page cheerfully said 'Payment successful'. Only an assertion on the order's charges -- not on the UI -- can see a double charge.

variants.hint: The page said 'Payment successful'. Did you check HOW MUCH was charged?
variants.debrief: The amount was computed with Math.trunc(19.99 * 100) = 1998 -- a one-penny undercharge on every order, because 19.99 * 100 is 1998.9999999999998 in floating point (Ch67 §8). Assert the exact charged amount in minor units.

variants.hint: After a decline, can the customer actually do anything? Try doing it.
variants.debrief: After a decline the Pay button stayed disabled, so the customer couldn't try another card. 'Shows an error' and 'lets the user recover' are different requirements -- test the recovery by recovering.

variants.hint: The page shows the decline correctly. What does the ORDER say about it?
variants.debrief: The server marked the order PAID before the gateway answered and never rolled it back on a decline -- a free parking fine. The UI was perfect; only the backend state revealed it.
